headline: Highest risk is data leakage: plano’s broad egress can exfiltrate caveman’s logs/notes if they share a workspace; prompt-injection and conflict risks are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and reads files like CLAUDE.md, project notes, and memory files; plano has broad network egress and can consume upstream outputs. If caveman content is routed into plano without provenance checks, injected instructions can cross the pair. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed.
conditions: IF caveman outputs are forwarded into plano prompts or routing inputs without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF a shared file or message channel carries untrusted text from caveman to plano, prompt hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding of caveman-generated text into plano prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all caveman outputs before plano consumes them.
Review any shared workspace files for instruction-like content before reuse.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between data and instructions.
requires-engineering: add allowlisted prompt templates in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while plano has broad network egress and sends requests to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If they share a workspace or logs, plano can transmit caveman-held sensitive context off-box. That is a plausible default-path exfiltration risk, though the shared workspace is not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF caveman and plano share any filesystem workspace or log directory, sensitive notes can flow into plano.
IF plano is configured with real traffic to its chat-completions endpoint, copied context may leave the host.
mitigations: Separate caveman and plano workspaces immediately.
Remove sensitive notes from any shared directory before running plano.
Restrict plano to redacted inputs only.
Check outbound requests from plano for unexpected payloads.
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation and egress filtering.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances, while plano does not. Both expose file surfaces and can operate on shared mutable artifacts, so concurrent writes or state stomping are plausible if orchestrated together. The profiles do not show locking or disjoint directories, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same config or notes directory, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator launches multiple caveman instances alongside plano on shared files, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each agent.
Run only one writer at a time on shared artifacts.
Back up shared files before concurrent runs.
Check for file diffs after each agent completes.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content-writing outputs and plano is a routing/gateway-style agent that can consume and forward model traffic. If plano treats caveman output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream requests or responses. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF plano uses caveman output as a prompt or routing decision without validation, errors can propagate.
IF caveman-generated text is reused in customer-facing or operational outputs, downstream mistakes multiply.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before plano consumes caveman output.
Require schema validation on caveman-produced text.
Compare critical facts against a second source.
Flag low-confidence caveman outputs for manual checking.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. caveman touches logs and notes, while plano touches logs and metrics, but the profiles do not show regulated data classes or conflicting policies. The other agent is cited because the risk is about policy mismatch across the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent without a shared policy, compliance review is needed.
IF one agent’s logs are retained longer than the other’s for the same data class, mismatch risk appears.
mitigations: Document a shared retention policy for both agents.
Avoid placing regulated data in either agent’s logs.
Confirm residency and vendor terms before deployment.
Purge logs after test runs.
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems.
